# loopcoder v0.6.0

0.6.0 is loopcoder's first breaking transition release. It ships model/depth discovery and validation, the new Google Antigravity provider path, the operator-visible reporter rename, and the 0.5.x to 0.6.0 upgrade/migration/doctor workflow.

## Upgrade from 0.5.x

Run the upgrade, inspect the repo, apply local repairs, then inspect again:

```text
loopcoder upgrade --version 0.6.0
loopcoder doctor --repo .
loopcoder doctor --repo . --fix
loopcoder doctor --repo .
```

`loopcoder upgrade` downloads the selected release, verifies signed `SHA256SUMS`, installs the binary, and refreshes the bundled loopcoder skill. The first `doctor` run is read-only. `doctor --fix` is the explicit mutating step for local migrations and cleanup. Environment variables cannot be edited by loopcoder, so move any old `LOOPCODER_CONDUCTOR_ATTEST_*` shell settings to the new `LOOPCODER_CONDUCTOR_REPORTER_*` names yourself.

## Breaking transition: reporter rename

New output uses the reporter vocabulary:

- `[reporter]` headers replace `[attestation]` headers.
- Result JSON uses `report` instead of `attestation`.
- Project hooks use `loopcoder hook conductor-reporter`.
- `.delivery.yml` uses `report.channel`.
- New env vars are `LOOPCODER_CONDUCTOR_REPORTER_SCOPE` and `LOOPCODER_CONDUCTOR_REPORTER_STATE_DIR`.

For one transition release, 0.6.0 still accepts old `[attestation]` tokens, old `attestation` result objects, the old `loopcoder hook conductor-attest` alias, old `.delivery.yml attestation` keys, and old `LOOPCODER_CONDUCTOR_ATTEST_*` env vars. New output and new writes use the reporter names only.

The invisible local machinery intentionally stays stable: `.loopcoder/relay/*.attest` files keep their extension, canonical report JSON field names such as `usage.total_tokens` are unchanged, and historical specs/changelog entries are not terminology-swept.

## Model and depth selection

`loopcoder models` prints the static registry for provider/model/depth choices:

```text
loopcoder models
loopcoder models --provider codex
loopcoder models --provider claude
loopcoder models --provider antigravity
```

Initial defaults:

| Provider | CLI | Default model | Default depth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `codex` | `codex` | `gpt-5.5` | `high` |
| `claude` | `claude` | `claude-opus-4-8[1m]` | `max` |
| `antigravity` | `agy` | `Gemini 3.1 Pro` | `High` |

Worker and Verifier selections are role-scoped. Each role resolves provider, model, and depth from one-run flags, `.delivery.yml`, then registry defaults. Invalid selections warn by default and pass through for compatibility; `models.strict: true` or per-run `--strict` rejects invalid selections before launch.

## Google Antigravity provider

The provider key is `antigravity`; the executable is `agy`.

```text
agy login
agy models
loopcoder models --provider antigravity
loopcoder doctor --repo .
```

The Worker invocation pins the target worktree explicitly:

```text
agy -p <prompt> --add-dir <worktree> --model "<model> (<Depth>)"
```

That `--add-dir` is required so Antigravity edits the worker worktree rather than its own scratch directory. Antigravity is a write-capable Worker provider. It is not a verified read-only Verifier or audit-review provider, so read-only selections fail closed.

## Doctor and local migration

`loopcoder doctor --repo .` is the read-only operational health report. It checks git, gh auth, configured provider CLIs, stable provider auth probes where available, `.delivery.yml`, model/depth validity, reporter/relay hook wiring, selected binary version, migration status, installed skill freshness, audit readiness, and stale local state counts.

`loopcoder doctor --repo . --fix` is the explicit repair mode. It may migrate legacy `attestation` config keys to `report`, rewrite eligible local state keys from `attestation` to `report`, refresh conductor hook settings from `conductor-attest` to `conductor-reporter`, migrate hook state labels, and prune stale gitignored local state under the retention policy. It does not log in to providers, flush pending relay obligations, edit tracked docs, choose models, commit, push, or mutate GitHub.

The cleanup policy retains active runs, recent runs, the newest retained run directories, pending relay obligations, recent and newest `.attest` relay ledgers, recent audit logs, referenced audit logs, and recent worktree-liveness artifacts. It is bounded, skips symlinks, and stays under `.loopcoder/`.

## Useful commands

```text
loopcoder models --provider antigravity
loopcoder dispatch --repo . --issue-number 595 --issue-title "..." --strict
loopcoder loopreview --repo . --pr-number 123 --provider claude --strict
loopcoder report --repo .
loopcoder doctor --repo .
loopcoder doctor --repo . --fix
loopcoder upgrade --version 0.6.0
```

See `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, and `docs/reference/usage.md` for the complete operator documentation.
